doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: A typical Cavett taping day
summary: Taping ran late afternoon, then everyone raced to evening record dates.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What was a typical day, how did it run for that show? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

We would tape in the afternoon. When I say afternoon, late afternoon. We’d start usually at 6 o’clock, something like that. Until 7:30. It was an hour show. And then everybody would run to an 8 o’clock or a 9 o’clock record date. It was just, we of course didn’t realize that eventually it would end. But all the people I played with last night, you know, we all did this together. It was the best of all possible worlds.
